policies.title: Kosovo: listed ordinary passports visa-free for a short visit
policies.summary: Kosovo's current MFA platform expressly lists these nationalities as not requiring a visa for entry, and the current Interior guidance sets the ordinary short-stay framework.
conditions: This is an ordinary-passport short-visitor classification, not an eVisa, ETA, or arrival-issued visa.

The current Interior guidance permits a foreigner to stay up to 90 days in every 180-day period visa-free or with a visa when required, subject to valid travel document, purpose, means, address registration, security and final-admission conditions.

The MFA platform separately permits some nationals to enter on a valid biometric identity card and permits Schengen-document holders to enter conditionally for 15 days. Those special-document substitutions do not broaden this passport-only list.

The live list retains Botswana, Namibia and Fiji although later PM decisions amend their visa regime. Botswana is outside this batch; Namibia is already canonical; Fiji is held pending proof of the signed amendment's Gazette publication.

policies.title: Kosovo: Hong Kong travel documents visa-free
policies.summary: Kosovo expressly exempts valid travel documents issued by the Hong Kong administration from the visa requirement.
conditions: This is document-specific to a valid travel document issued by the Hong Kong administration; it does not make a recognition, citizenship, diplomatic or other-document inference.
The same ordinary short-stay and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Kosovo: unlisted ordinary passports require an advance consular visa
policies.summary: Kosovo's MFA platform directs foreign nationals outside the named visa-free list and special document categories to apply for a Kosovo visa before a visit or transit.
conditions: Applications are made in person at the relevant Kosovo diplomatic or consular mission. The web contact form is not evidence of electronic visa issuance, and no eVisa, ETA, or passport-wide arrival-visa route is established.

The published process requires a completed original application and travel, purpose, accommodation or means, insurance and other supporting evidence. Possessing a visa does not itself guarantee entry.

A visa-regime national holding a valid biometric Schengen residence permit or valid multiple-entry Schengen visa can have a separate 15-day document-conditioned entry, transit and stay exemption. That condition does not change the ordinary-passport baseline.
Special diplomatic, official, refugee, stateless, UN/NATO/OSCE/EU travel-document, residence, work and identity-card routes are outside this classification.

application.label: Kosovo short-stay consular visa procedure
application.processingTime: Apply in person no later than three months before the visit; no decision-time promise is published.
steps: Apply in person to the relevant Kosovo diplomatic or consular mission.
Submit the completed original application, travel document, purpose and accommodation or means evidence, insurance and other requested documents.
Receive the visa decision before travel; possession of a visa does not automatically confer entry.

unresolved.reason: The current signed PM decision establishes Bosnia and Herzegovina short-stay entry only with a valid biometric identity card. It does not state the ordinary-passport rule, so no visa-free or advance-visa complement is inferred.

The signed December 2025 PM decision adds Fiji to the visa regime but makes effect conditional on Official Gazette publication. No current Gazette publication was confirmed, while the live MFA list still names Fiji visa-free.

Slovenia is absent from the MFA's listed passport-nationality schedule. The separate EU biometric-ID-card route does not directly establish an ordinary-passport rule, and omission is not normalized as advance visa.
